whyFeelPool: Estrogen and progesterone are both at their lowest — it's normal to feel low-energy, introspective, or a little tender these first few days.
Your body is doing real work right now. Many women feel more tired on period days, especially with cramps or heavy bleeding, so it's fine to go easier.
If you feel like slowing down, this is a good time to. If you feel fine, normal training is safe during your period.

whyFeelPool: Estrogen is climbing, bringing rising energy, sharper focus, and more motivation day by day.
Your body is rebuilding energy reserves right now — this is often the clearest-headed stretch of your whole cycle.
As estrogen rises, many women feel more up for new, harder or more social things. Notice whether that's true for you.

whyFeelPool: Estrogen peaks and a short LH surge triggers ovulation — energy, confidence, and sociability often peak right alongside it.
For many women this is one of the best-feeling weeks of the cycle, though it varies from person to person.
Testosterone also ticks up briefly around ovulation, which is part of why drive and confidence often feel sharper right now.

Peak energy is a resource — spend it deliberately, not just busily.

whyFeelPool: Progesterone rises then falls — it's common to feel more inward, hungrier, or more sensitive to stress as the phase goes on.
Your body temperature and resting heart rate rise a little this week, and many women feel more tired. A dip in energy is common and not a failure of willpower.
As progesterone falls late in this phase, mood and patience can dip — that's physiology, not a character flaw.
